subject.title: [Feature]: Pluggable STT backend for macOS Push-to-Talk

question: Should native macOS Push-to-Talk gain a batch STT backend boundary, and should that boundary reuse Gateway `tools.media.audio`/provider contracts or introduce a separate native app backend setting?
rationale: The request is valid but cannot be safely reduced to a settings toggle because maintainers must choose the owner boundary, endpoint/auth handling, private-network policy, fallback behavior, and partial-versus-final transcript UX.

options.title: Design native PTT batch STT seam
options.body: Add a maintainer-scoped native PTT transcription abstraction, keep Apple Speech as the default, and bridge to existing media/provider contracts where maintainers choose that owner boundary.

options.title: Fold into broader custom ASR design
options.body: Keep this issue as a narrower slice of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46661 and resolve both through one native ASR provider design.

options.title: Keep Apple Speech only for now
options.body: Defer custom native PTT transcription until security, UX, and provider-routing requirements are clearer.

recommendation.title: Design native PTT batch STT seam
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-scoped native PTT transcription abstraction, keep Apple Speech as the default, and bridge to existing media/provider contracts where maintainers choose that owner boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest native macOS voice history signal and is already mentioned in the issue timeline for this product area.
